defects: strip1-3 were missing, so the motion score rests only on frames.jpg and pairs.jpg
Lever shot transition: the headline 'One API call.' shows as abstract dashes and blobs mid-reveal, so the frame reads as a glitch rather than a designed in-between

The lever bank's glossy 3D look (red, blue and white handles, chrome knobs) breaks the flat schematic style used everywhere else and adds three off-palette colours
Tiny 'WEBHOOK' eyebrow labels (about 7px caps in green on dark green) are near the legibility limit and soft
Settlement shot: the trains on parallel tracks are evenly spaced and seem to move as a uniform conveyor (inferred from the pair), so it reads as a screensaver rather than a crowd with hierarchy

gaps: Motion is mostly linear translation and holds. There is no anticipation or settle on the train's arrival, no overlap between the signal turning green and the webhook card popping, and the handoffs between shots are blur dissolves rather than match-cuts built from the rail line, which is the device the whole film is built on

Pace and dead air: shots run 2.8 to 3.8 s, the webhook and opening yard shots sit almost static, and the busiest moment (many tracks) has a dense crowd but no focal choreography, so there is no clear climax beat before the converge-to-logo resolve

Sound is a dense, steady stream of percussive transients with one riser near 6 s. Dynamics are flat at -14 LUFS with no drop or breath at the end card, and no clear transients line up with the cuts or the SETTLED moment. Finish is also thin, with flat vectors and no material, light or texture to sell the railway-yard world
